subject: AI & Agents
title: AI in Drug Discovery
description: A micro-lesson that makes AI in Drug Discovery usable.

hook.text: It takes 10 years and $2.6 billion to develop one new drug. AI is cutting both numbers dramatically.

buildup.text: Traditional drug discovery screens millions of molecules through expensive lab experiments.

discovery.text: AI models predict which molecules will bind to target proteins without physical testing.

twist.text: AlphaFold solved protein folding — a 50-year biology puzzle — opening new drug targets.

climax.text: AI-designed drugs are now entering human clinical trials for the first time.

punchline.text: The next lifesaving pill might be designed by an algorithm.

quiz.question: How does AI speed up drug discovery?
options: By predicting effective molecules without physical testing

details.summary: AI accelerates drug discovery by predicting molecular interactions, identifying promising compounds, and simulating clinical outcomes. What once took years of lab work can be narrowed to months.
details.whyItMatters: Faster drug discovery means treatments reach patients sooner. AI is reducing costs and timelines in pharmaceutical research, potentially transforming healthcare access.
takeaways: AI predicts how molecules interact without physical experiments
Drug candidate identification has accelerated from years to months
Several AI-discovered drugs have entered clinical trials

faq.question: How does AI speed up drug discovery?
faq.answer: AI screens millions of molecular candidates virtually, predicting which ones will bind to disease targets. This narrows the field before expensive lab experiments begin, saving years and billions.

faq.question: Have any AI-discovered drugs reached patients?
faq.answer: Several AI-designed drug candidates have entered clinical trials. Insilico Medicine's AI-discovered drug for pulmonary fibrosis was one of the first to reach Phase II trials.
